title: Grafu: Unleashing the Full Potential of Future Value Computation for Out-of-core Synchronous Graph Processing
problem: Out-of-core graph systems using future value computation have significant gaps from optimality in IO reduction and incur substantial computation overhead and memory consumption. State-of-the-art systems fail to fully exploit future value computation while maintaining iteration-based dependency semantics.
motivation: As graphs grow exponentially, efficient out-of-core processing with optimized IO patterns is critical for handling large-scale graph analytics with synchronous programmable semantics.
method: Grafu maximizes future value computation by computing vertex values for future iterations in advance while respecting iteration-based dependencies. The system manages computation scheduling, IO prefetching patterns, and memory allocation to reduce IO accesses without violating synchronous semantics. It achieves this through careful orchestration of when and how future iterations are computed relative to current iteration boundaries.
key_novelty: First system to fully leverage future value computation for out-of-core synchronous graph processing while maintaining iteration-based dependency guarantees with optimized IO reduction.
contributions: Grafu system achieving near-optimal IO reduction through comprehensive future value computation
Reduced computation overhead and memory consumption versus state-of-the-art out-of-core systems
Methodology for scheduling future iterations within synchronous dependency constraints
